APP: solitaire-atelier
CURRENT PHASE: iterate_scope
PHASE PURPOSE: The app ALREADY exists and compiles in app_build. Decide exactly what to change to satisfy the latest requested change (see the '## Change requested' section of the prompt): which files to touch and what to add. Keep it minimal and preserve existing behavior. Do NOT rebuild from scratch.

===== ORIGINAL PROMPT (initial_prompt.md) =====
Build a native iOS Solitaire (Klondike) game — SwiftUI, 100% local, zero
network calls, zero sign-in/accounts/analytics/telemetry of any kind. No
backend. All state (stats, settings, saved game) persists on-device only.

THE CENTRAL CONSTRAINT — READ THIS FIRST: this must be a real, fully
playable, correctly-rules-implemented Klondike solitaire game. Drag-and-drop
(or tap-to-move) card interaction, legal-move validation, win detection,
undo, new-game/deal, and a stock/waste/foundation/tableau layout that
actually works. Do not let the visual ambition come at the cost of the game
being playable and correct — a beautiful app that can't be played is a
failure.

VISUAL DESIGN — THIS IS THE PART THAT MUST WIN AWARDS:
Cards must look like real, tactile playing cards — not the generic flat
rounded-rectangles-with-tiny-corner-pips that every solitaire clone uses.
Invent a genuinely original custom card face system: bespoke rank/suit
typography or iconography (not SF Symbols reused as suit glyphs), a
consistent illustrated or generative pattern language across all 52 cards
and the card back, real card-stock texture/shadow/lighting, and satisfying
physical motion (cards should feel like they have weight — spring-based
drag, believable flip/deal animation, subtle parallax or depth).

The bar: this should look and feel like something from an Apple Design
Award reel, not a tutorial app. Judge yourself against that bar throughout
— if a screen looks like a stock SwiftUI solitaire tutorial, it has failed
the brief. One clear, original visual "hook" (an art direction, a material
language, a signature interaction) should be identifiable in one glance
that no other solitaire app has.

Also include: light/dark mode (both fully art-directed, not just inverted
colors), haptics on card moves/wins, a stats screen (games played/won,
best time, streak — all local), and a settings screen (draw-1 vs draw-3,
card back selection, timer on/off).

Ship something that could realistically be submitted to the App Store today
and be visually distinctive in a screenshot alone.

## Change requested
The app currently FAILS its release gate: design lint: 22 design/dependency lint error(s) — e.g. inline_color at DesignSystem/Theme.swift:104 (hardcoded color — use a DesignSystem token). Full list in docs/design_lint.json. Fix every problem named until the gates pass; do not drop features unless unavoidable.
Full findings with file:line are in docs/design_lint.json — fix EVERY error entry.

===== DECISIONS LOG (structured, authoritative) =====
[...earlier context truncated...]

  rationale: CardView is more accurate since the same component renders the face-down back state, not just the front. Win and stuck need different iconography, tone, and action sets, and collapsing them into one type with an enum is exactly the kind of accidental simplification that already motivated keeping Stats' never-played/data-loss states structurally separate (DEC-design_discussion-005) — the same risk applies here. Conflating StatsModeFilter and DrawModeSetting into one shared ModeToggle component risked a real correctness bug: a draw-mode change slipping through without the confirmation dialog DEC-app_features-005 requires, since the Stats version has zero side effects and the Settings version mutates real game state.
  rejected: CardFaceView; A single merged TerminalOverlay component with an internal win/stuck enum; A single shared ModeToggle component used identically across Game header, Stats, and Settings
  constraints: Build phase must implement these as distinct named SwiftUI types, not variants of a shared type; Game screen must not include any draw-mode control; it lives only in Settings
- [DEC-design_handoff-004] Blocked/rejected-move feedback uses UIImpactFeedbackGenerator(.rigid) plus an 8-12pt one-cycle lateral shake; UINotificationFeedbackGenerator is reserved exclusively for the genuinely rare, significant session events — .success on win and .warning on stuck-board detection.
  rationale: Apple's own HIG guidance is that notification feedback should be used sparingly because frequent use dilutes its perceived meaning; a blocked-move tap is one of the most frequent events in casual play, especially for players still learning legal destinations, so using the heavier notification pattern there would feel naggy within a single session.
  rejected: UINotificationFeedbackGenerator(.warning) or .error for every blocked move
  constraints: All haptic trigger call sites must live in one shared interaction layer, not scattered through view code, per the existing haptics-verification requirement (DEC-prompt_contract-012)
- [DEC-design_handoff-005] Reduce Motion fallback is strict: a single 150ms linear opacity-only fade to final position, with zero positional translate and zero per-card stagger, applied identically to the deal sequence, the flip, and move-transit animations.
  rationale: Apple's Reduce Motion guidance targets parallax and positional motion effects specifically because even subtle translation can trigger vestibular discomfort for the people the setting exists for; a per-card stagger is itself a motion/choreography effect a Reduce Motion user is opting out of, not just asking to shorten.
  rejected: Opacity plus a subtle positional translate; A shortened but still spring-based or staggered deal sequence
  constraints: DealOrchestrator must branch on the Reduce Motion environment value once per session and apply this fallback uniformly to deal, flip, and move-transit, not per animation call site
- [DEC-design_handoff-006] Stats has no independent per-tab loading state; a single app-level hasFinishedInitialLoad flag, set once after Game/Stats/Settings all restore together at cold start, gates first paint across all three tabs.
  rationale: Once the one cold-start restore completes, Stats reads from an already-in-memory event log with no real async gap when a user taps the tab mid-session; specifying a separate per-tab loading state creates a dead code path that either never fires or, worse, risks getting stuck permanently visible if wired to the wrong lifecycle event — a real bug in the one area (Stats state honesty) this pipeline has repeatedly flagged as must-never-be-wrong.
  rejected: A dedicated per-tab Stats loading placeholder tied to its own async flag
  constraints: Build phase implements one shared hasFinishedInitialLoad flag from the single cold-start restore of GameSave.json, StatsLog.json, and Settings.json, not per-screen loading flags
- [DEC-design_handoff-007] Persisted state uses three independently-persisted files (GameSave.json, StatsLog.json, Settings.json), each with its own atomic temp-then-swap write, with a single @Observable GameEngine owning Game state, Stats reading from an append-only local event log the engine writes on game start/end, and Settings owning its own small struct.
  rationale: Physically separate files with independent atomic writes are what actually makes design_discussion's locked requirement (DEC-design_discussion-004: Game, Stats, and Settings each fail and recover independently) hold in practice — a single combined AppState.json would silently reintroduce a shared point of failure where a corrupt game save could take Stats or Settings down with it.
  rejected: A single combined AppState.json blob for all three screens' persisted state
  constraints: Build phase must implement three separate persisted files with independent atomic write-temp-then-swap operations, not a merged state file
- [DEC-design_handoff-008] The complete numeric design spec (type scale mapped to Dynamic Type styles, 4pt-base spacing grid, dual light/dark semantic color palettes with fixed card-color constants, corner radii, full component inventory, TabView-only navigation map, per-screen state models, motion/haptics tables, and accessibility rules) is locked as the single canonical handoff for the build phase, superseding both agents' earlier round-1 draft specs and partial component-name lists.
  rationale: The build phase needs exactly one spec with zero invented values and zero duplicate vocabulary; two competing drafts (differing on card color treatment, corner radius, component names, haptic types, and Reduce Motion behavior) would have forced the build phase to silently pick a side or fork into duplicate views.
  rejected: Handing off both agents' round-1 drafts and letting the build phase reconcile the differences
  constraints: Theme.swift must implement every token in this spec directly; no font/size/color/radius literals may appear elsewhere in the view layer
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] Core architecture is SwiftUI-only with one main-actor-isolated @Observable GameEngine owning board/undo/timer state, injected via @Environment from the App root, plus separate StatsLogStore and SettingsStore services — Apple frameworks only (SwiftUI, Foundation, Observation, UIKit haptics), no networking framework.
  rationale: Matches the already-locked three-independent-screen persistence model and keeps the app's only stateful mutation surface (GameEngine) isolated from Stats/Settings so a bug in one can't corrupt another; Apple-only frameworks satisfy the permissive-dependency policy with zero review risk.
  rejected: A shared combined app-state object across Game/Stats/Settings; Introducing any third-party state-management or networking library
  constraints: GameEngine must be main-actor-isolated; No URLSession or any networking API anywhere in the codebase
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] Persistence uses Codable + FileManager in Application Support (not SwiftData, not UserDefaults for game/stats/settings data), implementing the three-independent-file design (GameSave.json, StatsLog.json, Settings.json) via three separate dedicated actors, one per file, never a shared queue or shared actor.
  rationale: SwiftData's schema/migration machinery is pure overhead for three small Codable structs with no query or relationship needs; UserDefaults would needlessly widen the app's required-reason API surface; a shared write-scheduling actor would silently reintroduce the coupling the three-file split exists to prevent, just moved from the disk layer to the scheduling layer.
  rejected: SwiftData for game/stats/settings persistence; UserDefaults for game/stats/settings data; One shared PersistenceActor/queue serializing all three files
  constraints: Each of the three files must be written through its own independent actor performing temp-write-then-atomic-swap; No SwiftData dependency introduced for this app's persistence
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] The undo stack persists as part of GameSave.json itself (full-state log, capped at 200 entries, explicit schema version), not just the current board position.
  rationale: If only current board position survives a crash/jetsam kill, the app silently loses a core safety behavior the player already relies on ('I can always back out mistakes'), which directly contradicts this app's whole positioning of never lying about the player's own state.
  rejected: Persisting only the current board position and letting undo history reset on relaunch; A delta-based undo log instead of full-state snapshots
  constraints: GameSave.json must include a capped, versioned undo history; Full-state snapshots are used for determinism given the small per-entry size at this scale
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] Saves are event-driven and debounced: a write fires after every settling state mutation (move, undo, stock draw, timer toggle, session start/end), debounced ~300-500ms per file with a write-coalescing guard skipping no-op writes, plus an unconditional non-debounced flush forced on scenePhase background transition.
  rationale: A scenePhase-only save policy misses a foregrounded jetsam kill or crash after a move has already resolved, which this app has zero excuse to lose; but writing synchronously on every settling sub-event (e.g. a multi-card run relocation) risks I/O-induced stutter during the exact spring animations the app is built to protect, so the write is debounced while the in-memory engine state updates instantly.
  rejected: Saving only on scenePhase background transitions; Synchronous disk writes on every state-mutating event with no debounce
  constraints: In-memory GameEngine state must update immediately for UI regardless of debounce; Background transition must trigger an unconditional flush bypassing the debounce timer
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] The rank/suit legibility gate is verified via a required build artifact: a debug-reachable gallery view (or #Preview) rendering all 52 CardViews at the real computed cardWidth formula output, checked up through Dynamic Type accessibility1 before glyph shapes are treated as final.
  rationale: Five consecutive earlier phases flagged card-glyph legibility at true on-device size as an untested, release-blocking risk without ever specifying a concrete verification mechanism; 'check legibility before locking the glyph shapes' is not a testable requirement without a named artifact that must exist in the codebase.
  rejected: Leaving legibility verification as an unspecified manual check to happen 'at some point' during build; Judging legibility only from zoomed mockups instead of true on-device card width
  constraints: Build phase must implement this gallery/preview as an actual artifact in the codebase, gated behind #if DEBUG or an internal QA toggle; Verification must occur at the real cardWidth formula output, not a fixed or zoomed size
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] GameEngine's deal function accepts an injectable RandomNumberGenerator defaulting to the system RNG, used solely as a testing seam for deterministic unit-test fixtures; this seam must never be reachable from any production or UI code path.
  rationale: Enables deterministic unit tests (including hand-constructed adversarial draw-3 boards for stuck-detection false-positive testing) without touching the already-locked production rule that every new game uses a fresh real-RNG shuffle with no second deterministic RNG path.
  rejected: Wiring the injectable RNG to any debug menu or in-app control reachable by a user
  constraints: Production deal path must always default to the system RNG; No UI or settings surface may expose or reach the injectable RNG parameter
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] Testing strategy includes unit tests over all move-legality rules, win/stuck detection, and exact-state undo restoration; a randomized simulation/fuzz test running thousands of legal moves per draw mode asserting core invariants (52 unique cards always accounted for, foundation ranks never exceed 13, stuck-detection never fires while a legal move exists anywhere); XCUITest coverage of cold-launch deal, blocked-move feedback, both confirmation-sheet paths, and the two structurally distinct Stats states; explicit accessibility identifiers/labels on every custom-rendered view; and Xcode's performAccessibilityAudit() run inside the UI test suite.
  rationale: This is a fully custom-rendered UI with no system List/Form chrome, so none of it inherits accessibility identifiers or VoiceOver behavior automatically; a randomized simulation test is the only mechanism that actually makes the draw-3 'never falsely declare stuck' promise (DEC-app_features-002) verifiable rather than aspirational.
  rejected: Relying on hand-written unit tests alone without a randomized invariant-checking simulation; Treating accessibility as automatically covered because the app is built in SwiftUI
  constraints: Verification phases must run the randomized simulation and treat any invariant violation as a release blocker; All custom views require explicit accessibility identifiers for UI-test hooks, not just VoiceOver labels
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] Zero permission usage-description keys, zero entitlements beyond the sandbox default, zero background modes; persistence stays on FileManager rather than UserDefaults to minimize required-reason API surface; a PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy manifest is not authored by default but must be added declaring the specific usage if any code path later touches an actual required-reason API (e.g., reading a file's modification timestamp for stale/corrupt-save detection).
  rationale: Plain FileManager read/write does not itself trigger Apple's required-reason API rules — only specific API categories (file timestamps, disk space, boot time, etc.) do — so mandating a manifest purely because FileManager is used would add unnecessary noise; but the obligation must be tied to actual API usage so it isn't silently skipped if such a call is added later.
  rejected: Treating a PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy manifest as unconditionally mandatory from day one purely because FileManager is used; Ignoring the manifest requirement entirely regardless of future API usage
  constraints: No camera/location/photos/microphone/contacts/network permission keys may be added; If any required-reason API is introduced later, a manifest declaring that exact usage must be authored at that time
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] No App Tracking Transparency prompt and no NSUserTrackingUsageDescription key, stated as a deliberate non-requirement rather than an unaddressed gap.
  rationale: The app has genuinely zero tracking of any kind; naming this explicitly forecloses an engineer reflexively adding ATT 'just in case,' which would itself be an unnecessary permission prompt in a zero-permission app.
  rejected: Leaving ATT unaddressed and letting it be added speculatively later
  constraints: No ATT-related API or usage-description key may be added to this app
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] No ML/AR framework of any kind (CoreML, CreateML, ARKit, Vision) is in scope for this build, stated as a deliberate exclusion.
  rationale: Naming this explicitly forecloses a 'smart hint solver' or similar feature from sneaking in later as a disguised technical enhancement rather than an intentionally scoped addition requiring its own decision.
  rejected: Leaving ML/AR framework usage as an unaddressed, implicitly-open question
  constraints: Any future ML/AR feature proposal must be raised and scoped as its own decision, not treated as pre-approved
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] Zero StoreKit imports, zero payment capability, zero monetization-related entitlements — hard lock consistent with the already-locked no-monetization non-goal.
  rationale: Restates DEC-prompt_contract-010 and [REDACTED:high_entropy] at the architecture level so no StoreKit scaffolding or dead paywall code can regress into the codebase.
  rejected: Leaving StoreKit as an implicitly-absent rather than explicitly-excluded dependency
  constraints: No StoreKit framework import or payment capability may be added anywhere in the project
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] Zero third-party SwiftPM dependencies, enforced by an actual CI-checkable build step that fails if the project references any package beyond Apple's own frameworks, not merely a stated policy.
  rationale: This fleet has a documented history of shipping dependency-lint failures; a policy statement alone doesn't prevent regression the way an enforced build gate does.
  rejected: Relying on a written policy alone without an automated enforcement check
  constraints: CI must include a step scanning project/package references and failing the build on any non-Apple dependency
- [DEC-tech_specs-001] Card.id is a computed String property derived from suit+rank, never a stored Int or UUID field.
  rationale: Single-deck play (locked in prompt_contract) already guarantees suit+rank is a unique, stable identity for all 52 cards; a computed property is structurally excluded from Codable synthesis, so it can never be persisted incorrectly or drift from a save-file bug, which a stored deterministic value (even a derived one) technically still could. It also stays stable across isFaceUp toggling, which matchedGeometryEffect needs for the flip animation to read as one continuous view rather than a destroy/insert cross-dissolve.
  rejected: A stored UUID generated at deal time; A stored deterministic Int (e.g. suit.rawValue*13+rank.rawValue)
  constraints: Card must not gain any stored id field; id is always computed from suit+rank; AnimationStep.cardID and all card-keyed collections use this String id
- [DEC-tech_specs-002] PileID.foundation is keyed by Suit, not by an Int index.
  rationale: Makes 'exactly one foundation per suit' a compile-time invariant instead of a runtime bounds check; foundation(7) is simply unrepresentable.
  rejected: foundation(Int) with a 0..<4 runtime bounds check
  constraints: All foundation-indexed logic must pattern-match on Suit, never an array index
- [DEC-tech_specs-003] GameState carries no undo/history fields; the undo stack (GameStateSnapshot, full-state, capped at 200) lives only inside GameSaveFile as a plain LIFO stack with no redo cursor.
  rationale: Keeps GameState equality checks (used directly by the fuzz-invariant test suite) free of history bookkeeping, and avoids building a redo cursor field that no phase in this pipeline has ever asked for — a half-wired redo affordance is scope creep dressed as a data structure.
  rejected: Nesting undoStack/undoCursor inside GameState itself
  constraints: Undo pops via popLast() only; no redo mechanism may be added without a new decision reopening this one
- [DEC-tech_specs-004] Stats persist as a two-case append-only event stream (StatsEvent.gameStarted written immediately at session start, .gameEnded written on completion/abandonment), with DrawModeStats as a derived, incrementally-updated cache alongside the raw events rather than a per-render recomputation.
  rationale: A single end-of-session struct written only at game-end silently drops an entire session if the app is killed mid-game — exactly the failure mode this app's persistence architecture exists to prevent. Writing gameStarted durably at session start means an abandoned or crashed session still shows up as played instead of vanishing without a trace.
  rejected: A single StatsEvent struct written once at game completion; Recomputing DrawModeStats from the full event log on every StatsView render
  constraints: StatsLogStore.append must update both the event log and the relevant DrawModeStats cache in one write
- [DEC-tech_specs-005] RestoreIntegrityService performs a mandatory semantic validation pass (52 unique cards, no duplicate/missing ranks-per-suit, legal face-up stacking, foundation monotonicity) after every successful GameSave.json decode, returning ValidationResult (valid / invalid(reason:)); a failure is classified as PersistenceError.semanticallyInvalid and routed through the existing .dataLoss recovery path (fresh deal + dismissible banner), never silently activated as a resumed game.
  rationale: Atomic writes plus successful Codable decoding only proves the bytes round-tripped, not that the content describes a legal board; a subtle save bug or bit-level corruption could produce valid JSON describing an illegal board, which would then silently poison move-legality and stuck-detection with no visible error. A Bool-only validation result (the initial proposal) can't carry the failure reason the recovery banner needs for honest copy, so the return type must carry a reason string.
  rejected: Treating successful Codable decode as sufficient proof of a valid save; A Bool-returning validate() with no failure reason
  constraints: GameSaveStore.load() must call RestoreIntegrityService.validate before returning .restored; No new UI branch is added — semantic-invalid reuses the existing .dataLoss banner/recovery pattern
- [DEC-tech_specs-006] All three persisted files share one PersistenceStore protocol; each conforming actor returns RestoreOutcome<Model> directly from load() (restored / fallbackDefault / dataLoss) rather than throwing, and each actor owns its own independent serial write queue.
  rationale: Encodes design_discussion's required three-way recovery classification at the type level rather than leaving it to caller convention, while preserving the independent-failure guarantee (a slow/corrupt write to one file can never block or corrupt another) all the way from the file-format layer down to the write-scheduling layer.
  rejected: A protocol with an additional markRecovered() call with no clear caller once RestoreOutcome already carries the failure reason in-band; A single shared actor/queue serializing all three files
  constraints: GameSaveStore/StatsLogStore/SettingsStore each conform independently; no shared write queue
- [DEC-tech_specs-007] InteractionState is a locked, named finite-state enum (idle / sourceSelected / resolvingMove / dealing / terminal) that all Game-screen view code must read from; no parallel @State booleans for selection, highlight, or ambiguity may be introduced.
  rationale: Without a named FSM type, the natural build-phase shortcut is a handful of @State optionals for selected/highlighted/confirming, which is exactly the pattern that produces 'why didn't the highlight clear' class bugs — especially costly here since there's no menu screen to hide a rough edge behind.
  rejected: Ad-hoc @State booleans/optionals scattered across GameView for selection and highlight tracking
  constraints: GameView and all its subviews must derive selection/highlight/ambiguity rendering from GameEngine.interaction, not independent view state
- [DEC-tech_specs-008] DealOrchestrator/AnimationPlan is a locked, pure (side-effect-free) animation-planning layer that produces a declarative plan consumed by GameView via matchedGeometryEffect keyed on Card.id, covering fresh deal, flip, and multi-card run-relocation transit.
  rationale: A pure planning layer is unit-testable independently of whether SwiftUI actually renders it smoothly — 'did we compute the right animation sequence' and 'did it render smoothly' are different failure modes, and only the first is testable without a running app. matchedGeometryEffect keyed on stable card identity is also what makes a multi-card run relocation read as one coherent physical unit instead of N cards racing each other to nearby points.
  rejected: Independently-animated per-view offsets with no shared planning layer; Wiring animation logic directly and untested inside GameView
  constraints: DealOrchestrator must branch on Reduce Motion once per session and apply the locked strict opacity-only fallback uniformly across deal/flip/transit
- [DEC-tech_specs-009] Stuck detection is implemented as two separate, independently-testable types (DrawOneStuckDetector, DrawThreeStuckDetector) behind one StuckDetector protocol, selected by GameEngine based on the active draw mode.
  rationale: Operationalizes [REDACTED:high_entropy] and DEC-app_features-002, which already require draw-1's exact static pass and draw-3's conservative approximation to be distinct algorithms with different false-positive risk profiles; a single detectStuck() method would blur that distinction and make the two impossible to fuzz-test independently.
  rejected: A single GameEngine.detectStuck() method branching internally on draw mode
  constraints: The fuzz/simulation test suite must exercise both detector types independently, with a specific adversarial test proving DrawThreeStuckDetector never false-positives
- [DEC-tech_specs-010] Ambiguous-destination VoiceOver exposure is a named type, DestinationAccessibilityAction, built from InteractionState.sourceSelected's legalDestinations and wired as discrete .accessibilityAction entries.
  rationale: Operationalizes the already-locked requirement ([REDACTED:high_entropy], design_handoff accessibility rules) that a tap resolving to multiple legal destinations must expose each as a discrete VoiceOver action, not just a visual highlight — this had been stated as a requirement but never given a concrete type until this phase.
  rejected: Leaving ambiguous-destination VoiceOver exposure as an implementation detail with no named contract type
  constraints: CardView/PileSlotView must build their .accessibilityAction handlers from this type, driven directly off InteractionState
- [DEC-tech_specs-011] Module layout is locked as App/, DesignSystem/, Domain/, Persistence/, Features/Game/, Features/Stats/, Features/Settings/, Interaction/, DebugTools/, with Domain having zero dependency on SwiftUI or Persistence and Persistence knowing only Codable structs.
  rationale: This is the boundary that lets parallel build lanes work independently — Domain logic is fully unit-testable without a view hierarchy, and a persistence bug can't leak UI concerns or vice versa.
  rejected: A flatter structure without an enforced Domain/Persistence/UI dependency direction
  constraints: Domain/ must not import SwiftUI; Persistence/ must not import Domain's UI-facing types
- [DEC-project_plan-001] The card-glyph legibility gate (Theme tokens, CardGlyphs, CardView, CardGalleryDebugView) is sequenced as its own milestone that must close before gameplay UI (GameView/DealOrchestrator) construction begins, rather than being bundled into a later visual-polish milestone after gameplay UX.
  rationale: Building GameView and DealOrchestrator against unverified glyph shapes and a cardWidth formula risks broad rework across every consuming view if legibility fails at accessibility1 Dynamic Type; the legibility gate has been the pipeline's longest-standing unresolved risk and is cheapest to fail early.
  rejected: Codex's original ordering placing the full visual system (including card faces) as milestone 6, after gameplay UX in milestone 4
  constraints: Task-assignment phase must schedule CardGalleryDebugView's legibility pass to complete before any gameplay UI milestone begins consuming CardView/glyph shapes
- [DEC-project_plan-002] GameState's pile storage is changed from piles: [PileID: [Card]] to a named-field struct (stock, waste, foundations: [Suit: [Card]], tableau: [[Card]]).
  rationale: Swift's synthesized Codable for a non-String/Int-keyed dictionary (PileID has associated values) falls back to encoding as a flat alternating unkeyed array, producing non-inspectable JSON, non-guaranteed iteration order, and forcing RestoreIntegrityService to defensively iterate a dictionary instead of enumerating fixed fields.
  rejected: Leaving piles as a PileID-keyed dictionary as originally drafted in tech_specs' interfaces-json
  constraints: Domain milestone must include a round-trip Codable unit test for this structure before persistence work depends on it; RestoreIntegrityService and all pile-iterating logic must use named fields, not dictionary iteration
- [DEC-project_plan-003] On scenePhase background transition, the app must freeze/finalize elapsedSeconds (stop the timer) strictly before the unconditional persistence flush fires.
  rationale: Two independently-locked decisions (timer pauses on background; unconditional flush on background) were never sequenced relative to each other, creating a race that could persist a slightly-wrong elapsed time — exactly the class of 'app lied about the player's own data' bug this pipeline has repeatedly guarded against.
  rejected: Leaving the two lifecycle handlers unordered/independent
  constraints: Persistence/lifecycle milestone exit gate must implement and test this exact ordering
- [DEC-project_plan-004] Draw-3 stuck-detection verification requires hand-constructed adversarial board fixtures (a board with exactly one legal move buried in a specific stock-cycle position), in addition to randomized fuzzing, before the verification milestone is considered complete.
  rationale: Randomized fuzzing is much more likely to produce obviously-many-legal-moves or obviously-no-cards-left boards than the narrow 'exactly one buried move' case that would actually expose a false-stuck bug in the released 'never falsely reports stuck' promise.
  rejected: Treating randomized fuzz coverage alone as sufficient proof of the never-falsely-stuck guarantee
  constraints: Verification milestone must include a named adversarial fixture test suite for DrawThreeStuckDetector, distinct from the randomized invariant fuzz suite
- [DEC-project_plan-005] The undo-stack-in-GameSaveFile debounce window (~300-500ms) is documented as a floor that must not be lowered without a new decision re-evaluating I/O cost.
  rationale: Each debounced save serializes up to 200 full-state undo snapshots (roughly 100-200KB); naming the floor explicitly prevents a future 'make saves feel snappier' change from reintroducing I/O-induced stutter during the exact spring animations DealOrchestrator exists to protect.
  rejected: Leaving the debounce window as an unannotated tunable with no documented rationale
  constraints: Any change to the debounce interval must be logged as its own decision, not a silent tuning tweak
- [DEC-project_plan-006] Final build plan is locked as 8 sequenced milestones (Scaffolding/CI -> Domain Engine -> Persistence/Recovery -> Card Visual Foundation & Legibility Gate -> Gameplay UX -> Stats/Settings -> Lighting Scenes/Haptics Polish -> Verification & Repair) with explicit exit gates per milestone and an estimated 16-19 engineering days, including a dedicated verification-and-repair milestone rather than end-of-project polish.
  rationale: Combines Codex's milestone breakdown with the systems-risk resequencing and fixes (DEC-project_plan-001 through 005) into one executable plan satisfying the phase's required outputs: milestones, dependencies, risk mitigations, and a verification plan that isn't deferred to the end.
  rejected: Treating verification as end-of-project polish with no dedicated repair budget; Keeping Codex's original milestone ordering unmodified
  constraints: Task-assignment phase must follow this milestone order and dependency chain (Domain -> Persistence (parallel) -> Card Visual Foundation (hard gate) -> Gameplay UX -> Stats/Settings -> Lighting/Haptics -> Verification); Verification milestone must include the adversarial draw-3 fixtures and the backgrounding-ordering test named in this phase's decisions, not only generic fuzzing
- [DEC-task_assignments-001] Project scaffolds as a single Xcode project at SolitaireAtelier/ with one app target, one unit test target, and one UI test target, using exactly the module folder layout already locked in tech_specs — no new structure invented, folders assigned per the owning_lane tags already present in interfaces-json.

===== PHASE PLAYBOOK (editable phase_rules.json) =====
Global app-build rules:
- Prefer a smaller finished app over a larger half-built app.
- Every generated app must have real user-visible behavior, not only placeholder screens.
- For iOS apps, default to SwiftUI, deterministic local state first, Apple system frameworks, and no third-party package unless it materially reduces risk.
- Every screen needs empty, loading, success, and error states when the workflow can reach those states.
- No two text or control elements may visually overlap, collide, or clip each other. Labels never sit on top of values; values never stack into each other. When elements are positioned by a data value (times on a timeline, points on an axis), enforce a minimum gap and de-clutter (offset, group, collapse, or drop a colliding label) — overlapping text is a broken screen.
- The interface must never claim an outcome that has not happened: show Saved/Deleted/Sent/Synced/Unlocked only after it is truly confirmed, never a success state shown unconditionally. No sample or placeholder data shown as if it were the user's real data.
- Implement the design spec's tokens as one SwiftUI theme file (e.g. Theme.swift with type, spacing, and color definitions) and reference it everywhere; never scatter font/size/color literals through views.
- Every generated app must fully support dark mode: semantic color roles with explicit light and dark values, verified in both appearances.
- Empty states are designed content (icon + one-line explanation + the action that fills the screen), never a blank view or bare 'No data' text.
- No default unstyled List, Form, or navigation chrome where the design spec calls for custom rows, cards, or backgrounds; the built UI must match the spec.
- Treat accessibility, privacy, persistence, and testing as product requirements, not polish.
- Do not declare the app done until build verification and the final review agree on what works and what remains limited.

Phase rules:
- Scope the feature/fix precisely against the EXISTING app; change the minimum needed.
- Identify which existing files/interfaces are affected and what must NOT change.
- Define acceptance criteria for the change before building.

Required output:

- Affected files/interfaces and forbidden-edit zones.
- Acceptance criteria for the change.

Acceptance checks before consensus:
- The change is bounded, not a rewrite.
- Existing behavior outside scope is protected.
- Done is defined before building.

# iOS HIG + Native UX Cheatsheet (iOS 17+ / SwiftUI)

Rules for building iPhone apps that feel native and premium. Target iOS 17+, Swift 5.9+, SwiftUI-first, zero third-party deps. Snippets are idiomatic and compile on an iOS 17 deployment target unless a newer minimum is called out. When SwiftUI can't do it, drop to UIKit via `UIViewRepresentable`/`UIViewControllerRepresentable` — noted where relevant.

## Core principles (apply to every screen)

- **Prefer system components.** Native controls inherit Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, Reduce Motion, RTL, and dark mode for free. A custom control means you re-implement all of that or ship an inaccessible app.
- **Use semantic colors** (`Color.primary`, `.secondary`, `Color(.systemBackground)`, `.tint`), never hardcoded hex, so light/dark/increase-contrast modes work automatically.
- **Respect safe areas.** Let system spacing (`.padding()` with no argument) and `Spacer()` drive layout; avoid magic pixel numbers.
- **Use text styles** (`.font(.body)`, `.headline`, …), which scale with Dynamic Type. Fixed point sizes don't — avoid them for user-facing text.
- **One primary action per screen.** Everything else is secondary/tertiary in visual weight.
- **Latency budget:** any action >100ms needs feedback (spinner, skeleton, or optimistic UI). A measurable task >1s should show determinate progress.

## Navigation: pick the right container

Decision order — do NOT default to a sheet or a tab bar:

- **Tab bar (`TabView`)**: 2–5 top-level, peer sections the user switches between freely (Home, Search, Profile). Never for a linear flow or steps. Each tab persists its own navigation stack. Don't hide the tab bar mid-flow; if a screen needs full focus, present it modally instead.
- **Navigation stack (`NavigationStack`)**: drill-down into hierarchical content (list → detail → sub-detail). Push when the destination is a child of the current context and the user will want the back button + swipe-back.
- **Sheet (`.sheet`)**: a self-contained, interruptive task the user completes and dismisses (compose, filter, quick edit, share). Use detents for lightweight tasks. A sheet keeps the parent visible behind it — signals "you'll come right back."
- **Full-screen cover (`.fullScreenCover`)**: onboarding, media playback, camera, or a task that demands total focus with no parent context. Use sparingly — it breaks the "come right back" mental model.
- **Alert / confirmationDialog**: a decision, not a task. `alert` = 1–2 choices needing acknowledgment. `confirmationDialog` = a short list of actions (esp. destructive) anchored to what the user tapped.

Rule of thumb: if the user can be "in the middle of it" and navigate away, it's a stack. If they must finish or cancel, it's a sheet/cover. If it's a yes/no, it's an alert.

### NavigationStack with type-safe routing

Prefer value-based navigation over `NavigationLink(destination:)` — it enables deep linking, programmatic pop-to-root, and state restoration.

```swift
enum Route: Hashable {
    case detail(itemID: UUID)
    case settings
}

struct RootView: View {
    @State private var path: [Route] = []
    let store: ItemStore

    var body: some View {
        NavigationStack(path: $path) {
            List(store.items) { item in
                NavigationLink(value: Route.detail(itemID: item.id)) {
                    ItemRow(item: item)
                }
            }
            .navigationTitle("Items")
            .navigationDestination(for: Route.self) { route in
                switch route {
                case .detail(let id): DetailView(itemID: id)
                case .settings:       SettingsView()
                }
            }
        }
    }

    func popToRoot() { path.removeAll() }
    func openSettings() { path.append(.settings) }
}
```

- `.navigationTitle` goes on the content, not the stack. Large title for top-level roots (default), `.inline` for pushed detail screens where a large title wastes space:

```swift
.navigationBarTitleDisplayMode(.inline)
```

- Toolbar placement is semantic, not positional — the system positions it correctly for the platform + RTL:

```swift
.toolbar {
    ToolbarItem(placement: .topBarLeading) { Button("Cancel") { dismiss() } }
    ToolbarItem(placement: .primaryAction) { Button("Save", action: save) }
    ToolbarItemGroup(placement: .bottomBar) { EditButton(); Spacer(); addButton }
}
```

(`dismiss` comes from `@Environment(\.dismiss) private var dismiss`.)

### TabView

```swift

    @State private var selection: Tab = .home
    enum Tab: Hashable { case home, search, profile }

    var body: some View {
        TabView(selection: $selection) {
```
